claim: For every nondegenerate convex quadrilateral \(Q\) with diagonal-intersection shorter-to-longer ratios \(p,q\in(0,1]\), the point-inversion Minkowski asymmetry satisfies \[s(Q)=1+\frac{1-pq}{1+\min\{p,q\}}.\] Its Minkowski center is unique; after affine normalization \(Q=\operatorname{conv}\{(1,0),(0,1),(-p,0),(0,-q)\}\) with \(0<p\le q\le1\), it is \[c=\frac{(s(Q)-1,1-q)}{s(Q)+1}.\] The attainable range is \([1,2)\), and \(s(Q)=1\) exactly for parallelograms.
integrity: First public source date independently confirmed from arXiv version history. Proof and rational checker reproducible. No claim of independent verification or bibliographic exhaustiveness.
scientific_limitations: Only nondegenerate convex quadrilaterals; affine normalized center, not Euclidean invariant coordinates. No formula for general polygons; historical priority uncertainty remains. Analytic four-facet proof; exact rational testing is supplemental.
title: Exact Minkowski asymmetry and the unique center of every convex quadrilateral
